payout_quote: Find rebates and special offers near you on ENERGY STAR certified products. (Federal 25C cooling-equipment credit: expired for property placed in service after December 31, 2025.)
timing: Utility rebates are typically paid 4-8 weeks after the cooling equipment is installed and documented. The federal 25C credit is closed for 2026 installations.
eligibility: Set by each utility program: generally must be a residential customer; cooling equipment (central AC, heat pump, smart thermostat) must meet the program's efficiency specifications; some programs require pre-approval before purchase.
catches: The federal tax credit for efficient cooling equipment (25C) EXPIRED December 31, 2025.
Remaining rebates are utility-specific and vary by location; amounts are typically $25-$300, not $500.
You must buy the equipment first — this is a discount on spending, not money earned.
Some programs require pre-approval before purchase.
steps: Look up cooling rebates for your zip code at https://www.energystar.gov/rebate-finder and https://dsireusa.org.
Open your utility's specific offer and confirm it is live, the qualifying equipment specs, and any pre-approval requirement.
Buy and install the qualifying cooling equipment or smart thermostat and keep receipts.
Submit the rebate application with proof of purchase; the rebate arrives as a bill credit or check, typically in 4-8 weeks.
biggest_catch: The federal credit for efficient cooling equipment expired December 31, 2025 — what's left are utility rebates (typically $25-$300) that require buying the equipment first; it is a discount, not income.
notes: CORRECTION vs the route: the old federal 25C cooling credit is gone; 2026 reality is utility rebates in the tens-to-low-hundreds. Verified via the live EPA finder and DSIRE 2026-09-22. PRODUCT NOTE: cooling rebates are purchase discounts, not earnings.
